summary: Boundary County lookout: 40-foot pole L-4 tower, staffed one week, torn down 1959; FFLA lists it as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: FFLA list shows the tower as gone; no source describes what remains on the site today

events.note: 40-foot pole L-4 tower. Two sources give 1941; Forest Lookouts says 1930s with CCC labor.

evidence.supports: about 10 miles east of Nordman in Boundary County
40-foot pole L-4 tower, built 1941, manned one week, torn down 1959
evidence.quote: Named for Ranger Leslie E. Eddy, this 40' pole L-4 tower, built in 1941, was manned for only one week. It was torn down in 1959.

evidence.supports: named for Ranger Leslie E. Eddy
evidence.quote: Named for Ranger Leslie E. Eddy

evidence.supports: 1941 build date and 40-foot pole L-4 tower (Idaho Fire Lookouts)
Forest Lookouts says built in the 1930s with Civilian Conservation Corps labor
evidence.quote: 1930's: The Eddy Creek lookout tower was erected using Civilian Conservation Corps labor. (Payette Valley Sentinel)

evidence.supports: agency is the Priest Lake Timber Protective Association
Priest Lake TPA is the agency named on firelookout.com (abbreviated)
FFLA list marks Eddy Peak as tower gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1941; Forest Lookouts says the 1930s with CCC labor. Story reports both; the event uses 1941 from two sources.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts (1941 vs 1930s). A geocaching listing says remains are still on the site; its page cached as title only, so not quoted or used. Access and current ownership not in the sources. Staffing as_of 1959 is inferred from torn-down date plus one-week staffing. Record had design and height null; both now filled from two sources (40 ft = 12.2 m). Forest Lookouts quotes the Payette Valley Sentinel calling it the Eddy Creek lookout tower; the story attributes the 1930s/CCC claim to that page without asserting the name. The access advice was changed: no source covers access or current ownership, so the story no longer names PLTPA as the contact.
